failures.criterion: Filter drift (spec): the committed coverage check fails, naming each uncovered file, when a job reads a file its filter misses. This is the round-3 finding (a package added to a go command the table claims) in two forms the round-4 fix still lets through
failures.evidence: line_packages (ci_filter_coverage.py:353-367) counts only relative patterns (`./x`, `../x`) after `go <subcommand>` on the same physical line, and go_lines reads one line at a time. So a package appended by its import path, or on a backslash-continued next line, is never put through go list. Probes on ci.yaml:2246 at 84618fbf, each reverted after: (a) `go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 20m -v ./cmd/broker github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/routing` -> check-ci-filters.sh exits 0, 'broker-multiprocess: 278 files, 0 uncovered'; (b) `run: |` with `go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 20m -v ./cmd/broker \` then `  ./internal/routing/` on the next line -> exits 0, the same line. In both cases broker-multiprocess would test internal/routing, whose files its filter does not match (round 3: PathsFilter(broker_multiprocess).covers('packages/envoy/internal/routing/match.go') is False). The relative form on the same line is refused: exit 1. Red tests, commit 0c15655f on legion/INFRA-520, in .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.test.sh: the case 'a package added to a claimed go command by its import path, outside the job's filter' (the fixture runs `go test ./cmd/app ./lib example.com/m/other`) and the case 'a package added to a claimed go command on a continuation line, outside the job's filter' (`go test ./cmd/app ./lib \` / `./other`). Each expects exit 1 and output naming other. Command: `PATH=<python with PyYAML>:$PATH bash .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.test.sh` -> 'Results: 38 passed, 4 failed'. Both fixtures exit 0 today, so their YAML and go commands are valid. Fix: join backslash-continued lines before reading a go command, and refuse (fail closed on) any positional argument of a claimed go command that is neither a flag, a flag's value, nor one of the Run's packages, instead of counting only `.`-prefixed tokens.
